_comment: Vendoring scope policy for shared-core/tooling/. tools/vendor.js enforces it and records every exclusion in manifest.json; test/install.test.js re-checks the shipped tree against these same terms. The rule: this package is published, so it carries PERSONAL tooling only, and nothing that names machine paths or an employer's internal systems. Archived-on-machine is not the same as published: everything removed is still archived locally under ~/.config/asb-mods/backups/<stamp>/ regardless of this policy.

scan.homePath: derived at runtime from $HOME (never written into a shipped file)
scan.note: The literal employer term list stays off the public package: it is read from the git-ignored policy.local.json when present. Mechanism ships, vocabulary does not.

denyBundles.reason: Employer-internal agent definitions. Not personal tooling.

denyBundles.name: org-index
denyBundles.reason: Employer-internal source-org indexing pipeline and its per-repository digests.

denyBundles.name: atelier-panel-session-scope.test.mjs
denyBundles.reason: Single-file test with an absolute author home path baked in.

denyBundles.name: pi-wf
denyBundles.reason: Prompts/skills/scripts reference the employer-internal onboarding pipeline in source.

denyBundles.name: pi-session-model-sync
denyBundles.reason: Source names employer-internal model refs and paths.

denyBundles.name: pi-session-learnings
denyBundles.reason: Source routes learnings into employer-internal knowledge systems.
Plugin installs and their registries (installed_plugins.json, marketplace/catalog caches) are third-party state: Claude Code rebuilds them when the plugins are reinstalled.
Hook directories belong to third-party plugins; this package registers its own hooks via shared-core/hooks instead.

restoreNote: Excluded bundles are still removed by the cutover and still archived; on THIS machine restore them with `asbmods reset`. They are simply absent from what a fresh machine gets from the published package, which is why `status` prints the exclusion list.
unlistedNote: A skill or loose file not declared in personalSkills/personalCodexFiles is treated as third-party or employer content: it stays archived on this machine and is reinstalled from its upstream source (npm package, marketplace, or the employer) rather than redistributed by this package.
denyBundlesNote: denyBundles reasons state the category only; the specific internal systems are named in the git-ignored policy.local.json denyReasons map, keyed '<cls>:<name>'.
